newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam trade gap narrows, industrial output up.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam trade gap narrows, industrial output up.

text.p: Vietnam said on Friday its first-half trade deficit for 1997 was expected to register at $1.432 billion, lower than in the same period of 1996 when the gap between imports and exports reached $1.77 billion.

Data issued by the General Statistics Office showed also that industrial production for the period was up at a year-on-year rate of 13.6 percent. In the first half of 1996 the year-on-year increase was 13.2 percent.

Exports for the period reached $4.1 billion while imports stood at $5.532 billion. The office said the figures represented an increase in exports of 30.2 percent while imports were up just 0.3 percent.
Separate data for the month of June showed a deficit of $266 million, compared to $230 million in May. Imports stood at $1.0 billion and exports amounted to $734 million.

A breakdown of the industrial output figures for the first half of this year showed increases in the state-owned sector at 10.7 percent, 10.0 percent in the non-state sector, and 23.0 percent in the foreign invested sector.

The June industrial output rate registered an increase of 13.3 percent compared to the same month last year, with growth of 10.4 percent in the state-owned sector, 8.9 percent in the non-state sector, and 23.9 percent in the foreign-invested sector.
